parsed.explanation: Thin dossier extrapolated from structure: both competing frameworks criminalise same-sex intimacy with up to 3 years' imprisonment, camp officials are documented holding prisoners on homosexuality charges without courts, the administering state's courts/detention operate on political cases, and there is documented no protection against discrimination or violence with high social exposure. No trans-specific visitor case, facilities, document or care rule is documented, so no trans-specific targeting is proven, but the criminal lever, absent recourse and hostile social framing mean outing risks imprisonment, not mere friction. Uncertainty and absence of protections keep this well below acceptance tiers.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Administering state operates security services, courts and detention; same-sex law carries 6 months to 3 years. Camp officials held prisoners on homosexuality charges without court process.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Criminal prohibition in either part means framework choice does not remove detention exposure if read as same-sex conduct.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Same-sex intimacy criminalised under both frameworks up to 3 years; colonial inheritance unrepealed until later. Social exposure high: Muslim majority, same-sex relationships read as foreign phenomenon.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Movement constitution silent; 2010 diplomat said it does not punish, but silence is not decriminalisation and no statute decriminalises.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Secondary sexuality-law lever combines with no legal protection and disputed, non-court camp administration; trans-specific application is unsourced.

minors_guardians.interaction: No age-specific rule documented; minor does not remove adult's criminal or detention exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented trans-specific violence case; general exposure inferred only from no protection against discrimination or violence and foreign-phenomenon framing.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Refugee-aid body states no type of protection for LGBTQ people against discrimination or violence.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Documented camp detention and political-case courts suggest recourse for outed visitors is weak, but street-violence rate is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No remedy documented; 2005 defenders' trial called dubious by human-rights organisation, showing courts used for political cases.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin data on documents, facilities, care and trans-specific application resolves toward structural risk from criminalisation and no relief, not toward midpoint.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in routine state contact without credible execution, but this case is lower: 0.35-B has hours-long checks, fines and no imprisonment, while here statute allows up to 3 years and camp detention without courts is documented, with no working remedy shown.

Similar or slightly higher: 0.25-D has morality law selectively applied to trans people, entrapment/blackmail, short jail and some appellate annulments. Here trans-specific application is not documented, but imprisonment range and no-protection record keep it near this tier or below it.

Higher than this case: 0.55-B is mainly administrative secondary screening, refused admission and slow appeals without criminal imprisonment. Here criminalisation with custodial penalties and non-court detention, plus hostile social exposure, is materially more severe.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is one criminalising system under two administrations: administering-state courts/detention on most ground and camp-based detention in exile, both prohibiting same-sex intimacy up to 3 years. No documented trans-specific visitor targeting, facilities or care exposure, but also no protection, decriminalisation or remedy. Extrapolating from criminalisation, disputed governance, political-case courts and camp detention, an outed visitor faces arrest/imprisonment risk and social hostility without recourse, while execution and routine trans-presentation sweeps are not documented. That places it in High Risk, above 0.15 anchors requiring documented beating/routine arrest for presentation, below 0.35 anchors where consequences stop at exclusion/fines.
